raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The Qwen3 cookbook covers datacenter GPUs, Intel Arc, and Xeon, but has no guidance for 16 GB consumer cards, where the default KV pool is the main limit. This was discussed in #46804, where measuring and adding a 3.2 config-tip bullet was suggested as the low-friction route.

## Modifications

Adds one bullet to section 3.2 (Configuration Tips) of `docs/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.mdx`:
- On a 16 GB card, `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8` with default flags gets a ~16K-token KV pool, compared with a 40,960-token default context.
- `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` doubles the pool. The bullet gives the measured TTFT/TPOT trade-off and the GSM8K comparison, so readers can judge the accuracy cost.
- The scheduler reserves KV based on `max_tokens`, clipped at `SGLANG_CLIP_MAX_NEW_TOKENS_ESTIMATION` (default 4096). It covers the client cap and the server-side env var.
- It links the open pip-install issues on recent toolchains.

The command generator (`qwen3-deployment.jsx`) is unchanged. The FP8 KV flag is lossy, so it lives only in the tip and not in a generated cell. The command in the bullet uses `sglang serve`.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K with sgl-eval 0.1.3, using Qwen3's recommended non-thinking settings (sgl-eval has no Qwen3 preset):
`sgl-eval run gsm8k --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 --num-examples 200 --n-repeats 3 --chat-template-kwarg enable_thinking=false --temperature 0.7 --top-p 0.8 --max-tokens 4096 --seed 0`

| config | pass@1 (3 repeats) | std | majority@3 |
|-|-|-|-|
| default (BF16 KV) | 0.955 | 0.015 | 0.963 |
| `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` | 0.938 | 0.008 | 0.950 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Environment: RTX 4070 Ti SUPER (SM89, 16 GB), driver 610.88, WSL2, glibc 2.43, sglang `0.5.6.post3.dev13281+gdea05ca16` (main), torch 2.14.1+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2, Triton 3.8.0. All runs were cache-cold.

bench_serving uses the page's 5.1.1 commands plus `--flush-cache` (`--dataset-name random --random-input-len 1000 --random-output-len 1000`):

| config | c | median TTFT | P99 TTFT | median TPOT | output tok/s |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| default (BF16 KV) | 1 | 36 ms | 105 ms | 17.6 ms | 56.5 |
| `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` | 1 | 36 ms | 106 ms | 17.6 ms | 56.5 |
| default (BF16 KV) | 16 | 1159 ms | 7448 ms | 26.4 ms | 458 |
| `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` | 16 | 126 ms | 652 ms | 28.6 ms | 490 |

The max_tokens/admission sweep (128 concurrent short-answer requests, same output length in every arm) and its script are in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions/46804. At the default bf16 pool, raising the client cap from 256 to 4096 cuts peak running requests from 23 to 9, while 8192 matches 4096 because of the clip. `SGLANG_CLIP_MAX_NEW_TOKENS_ESTIMATION=1024` with a client cap of 8192 matches a client cap of 1024.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (Docs only)
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch:
@@ -47,6 +47,10 @@ import { Qwen3Deployment } from "/src/snippets/autoregressive/qwen3-deployment.j
 - **Expert Parallelism:** SGLang supports Expert Parallelism (EP) via `--ep`, allowing experts in MoE models to be deployed on separate GPUs for better throughput. One thing to note is that, for quantized models, you need to set `--ep` to a value that satisfies the requirement: `(moe_intermediate_size / moe_tp_size) % weight_block_size_n == 0, where moe_tp_size is equal to tp_size divided by ep_size.` Note that EP may perform worse in low concurrency scenarios due to additional communication overhead. Check out [Expert Parallelism Deployment](../../../docs/advanced_features/expert_parallelism) for more details.
 - **Kernel Tuning:** For MoE Triton kernel tuning on your specific hardware, refer to [fused_moe_triton](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton).
 - **Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B on H200:** For concurrent requests with long prompts, benchmark `--enable-mixed-chunk` to mix decode requests into chunked-prefill batches. This can reduce median time to first token (TTFT), but may increase time per output token (TPOT) and end-to-end tail latency. Compare these metrics and throughput on your workload before enabling it.
+- **Qwen3-8B on 16 GB consumer GPUs (e.g. RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, SM89):** With default flags, `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8` leaves room for a KV pool of only about 16K tokens, well below the default 40,960-token context, so concurrent requests start queueing early. `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` doubles the pool in the same memory. On an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER at 16 concurrent requests (random 1000/1000), it cut median TTFT from 1.16 s to 0.13 s, with about 8% higher TPOT. Check accuracy on your workload: GSM8K (sgl-eval, 200 examples × 3 repeats, non-thinking) was 0.938 with FP8 KV, compared with 0.955 with BF16 KV. On a small pool, the scheduler also reserves KV for each request based on its `max_tokens`, up to `SGLANG_CLIP_MAX_NEW_TOKENS_ESTIMATION` (default 4096). Clients that send a large `max_tokens` but get short answers therefore lower concurrency. Cap `max_tokens` on the client, or lower that variable on the server. Pip installs on recent toolchains have open issues: [#43591](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/43591), [#46420](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46420), [#45066](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/45066).
+  ```shell Command
+  sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3
+  ```
 - **Speculative Decoding:** Using Speculative Decoding for latency-sensitive scenarios.
   - `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE3`: Speculative decoding algorithm
   - `--speculative-num-steps 3`: Number of speculative verification rounds
